name: Technologies: GraphQL
description: GraphQL schemas, queries, mutations, and when to choose it over REST.

cards.subject: An object type
says: declares a named set of fields, each with its own type
is the main building block of a schema
cards.use: want to describe an entity such as a User with its fields
not: stores rows of data inside the schema itself

cards.subject: A scalar type
says: is a leaf value that has no sub-fields
includes the built-ins Int, Float, String, Boolean and ID
cards.use: need a field that returns a plain value rather than an object
not: must be queried with a nested selection set

cards.subject: The non-null marker
says: is written as an exclamation mark after a type
promises the server will never return null at that position
makes a field required when placed on an argument that has no default
cards.use: want to guarantee that a field always has a value
not: checks the value against a database constraint

cards.subject: The list modifier
says: wraps a type in square brackets to return many values
can be combined with non-null on the items, the list, or both
cards.use: need a field that returns several values of one type
not: limits the list to ten items by default

cards.subject: An enum
says: restricts a field or argument to a fixed set of named values
is serialised as the value name in a JSON response
cards.use: want a field limited to values such as ACTIVE or CLOSED
not: can hold values of different types at once

cards.subject: An interface
says: declares fields that every implementing object type must include
lets a field return different object types that share a set of fields
cards.use: want several types to share fields and still be returned from one field
not: lets implementing types leave out declared fields

cards.subject: A union type
says: groups object types that need not share any fields
can only contain object types as members
needs an inline fragment to select fields of a member
cards.use: want a search field to return either a User or a Post with nothing in common
not: can include scalar types as members

cards.subject: An input object type
says: groups several arguments into one structured value
can only contain fields that are scalars, enums or other input types
cards.use: want a mutation to accept one structured argument
not: can be returned from a query field

cards.subject: A custom scalar
says: adds a leaf type such as DateTime with its own parsing and serialising rules
keeps its validation logic in server code instead of in the SDL
cards.use: need a leaf value such as a timestamp that the built-in scalars cannot express
not: is validated automatically by the SDL declaration alone

cards.subject: The Query root type
says: holds every entry point for reading data
is the only root type a schema must define
cards.use: want to know where all read operations begin
not: is optional in a schema

cards.subject: The Mutation root type
says: holds the entry points that change data
is optional in a schema
cards.use: want to find where write operations are declared
not: is required in every schema

cards.subject: A field argument
says: is declared in parentheses after a field name in the SDL
can carry a default value in the schema
cards.use: want a field to accept a filter or an id
not: can only be placed on root fields

cards.subject: A query
says: reads data and is not meant to cause side effects
may have its sibling root fields resolved in parallel
cards.use: want to fetch a user together with their posts
not: executes its top-level fields strictly one after another

cards.subject: A mutation
says: changes data on the server
executes its top-level fields serially, in the order written
cards.use: need to create, update or delete a record
not: runs its top-level fields in parallel for speed

cards.subject: A subscription
says: keeps a connection open so the server can push events
is commonly carried over WebSocket or server-sent events
cards.use: want the client to be told when new messages arrive
not: is answered with one response and then closed

cards.subject: A variable
says: is declared in the operation with a dollar sign and a type
is sent in a JSON map separate from the query text
cards.use: want to reuse one query with different values safely
not: must be spliced into the query string before sending

cards.subject: A fragment
says: names a reusable set of fields on a given type
is included in a selection with three dots and its name
cards.use: repeat the same fields in several places in a document
not: is sent to the server as a separate request

cards.subject: An inline fragment
says: applies a type condition inside a selection set without a name
is how fields of one union member are selected
cards.use: need to read fields that exist only on one member of a union
not: must be declared as a separate named definition

cards.subject: An alias
says: renames a field in the response
lets one field be requested twice with different arguments
cards.use: want two results from the same field in one query
not: renames the field in the schema

cards.subject: An operation name
says: labels a query for logs and tooling
selects which operation runs when a document contains several
cards.use: want to identify a query in server traces
not: is required for every anonymous shorthand query

cards.subject: The @include directive
says: adds a field only when its if argument is true
takes a Boolean that is often supplied by a variable
cards.use: want to fetch an expensive field only when a flag is set
not: removes the field when its if argument is true

cards.subject: The @skip directive
says: leaves a field out when its if argument is true
is the inverse of the include directive
cards.use: want to omit a field when a flag is set
not: adds the field only when its if argument is true

cards.subject: A selection set
says: lists the wanted fields inside curly braces
is required on any field that returns an object type
cards.use: need to name the fields the response should contain
not: is optional on object-valued fields

cards.subject: A variable default value
says: is used when the client does not send that variable
is declared next to the variable's type in the operation
cards.use: want an optional page size to fall back to a safe number
not: overrides a value the client did send

cards.subject: The __typename meta field
says: returns the name of the object type at that position
tells apart members of a union or interface in a response
cards.use: need to know which concrete type came back
not: must be declared in the SDL of each type

cards.subject: A resolver
says: is the function that produces the value of one field
runs per field while the response tree is built
cards.use: need a field to read from a database or another service
not: produces the whole response for the entire query

cards.subject: The parent argument
says: holds the value returned by the enclosing field's resolver
is the root value for fields on the root types
cards.use: need a nested field to use data already loaded by its parent
not: contains the arguments sent by the client

cards.subject: The context object
says: is created once per request and shared by all resolvers in it
is the usual home of the authenticated user and data loaders
cards.use: want every resolver to see the caller identity
not: is built separately for each field

cards.subject: The info argument
says: carries the parsed operation and schema details for the current field
exposes the selected sub-fields for look-ahead optimisations
cards.use: want a resolver to see which columns the client asked for
not: holds the authenticated user

cards.subject: The default resolver
says: reads the property named like the field from the parent object
means trivial fields need no resolver code
cards.use: have a field whose name matches a property of the returned object
not: is replaced by an error when no resolver is given

cards.subject: The validation phase
says: checks a parsed document against the schema before any resolver runs
rejects unknown fields and wrong argument types
cards.use: want malformed queries rejected without touching data
not: runs after the resolvers have finished

cards.subject: The execution phase
says: walks the selection set and calls resolvers
coerces each resolved value to its declared type
cards.use: want to see where resolver errors are collected
not: rejects documents that mention unknown fields

cards.subject: Null propagation
says: turns a null in a non-null field into a null of the nearest nullable parent
can null an entire list item or object
cards.use: see a whole parent object vanish after one non-null field failed
not: always fails the whole request with no data

cards.subject: Abstract type resolution
says: decides which concrete object type an interface or union value is
is needed whenever a field returns an interface or union
cards.use: need the server to name the concrete type of a returned value
not: is skipped when the client uses a fragment

cards.subject: Variable coercion
says: converts the JSON variable values to the declared input types
fails the request before execution when a variable has the wrong type
cards.use: see an error for a variable sent as the wrong type
not: is performed separately by each resolver

cards.subject: The N+1 problem
says: runs one query for a list and one more query per item for a nested field
appears when each resolver loads its own data independently
cards.use: see fifty author lookups after loading fifty posts
not: is caused by using too many mutations

cards.subject: A DataLoader
says: collects the keys requested within one tick and fetches them in one batch
memoises results per key for the lifetime of the instance
cards.use: need to turn many single-key lookups into one batched call
not: splits one large batch into many single lookups

cards.subject: A per-request DataLoader
says: is created inside the context for each request
prevents cached data from leaking between users
cards.use: must avoid sharing cached results across different callers
not: is shared by all requests for speed

cards.subject: A query depth limit
says: rejects documents nested deeper than a set number of levels
blocks cyclic queries such as author, posts, author, posts
cards.use: face clients writing deeply nested cyclic queries
not: measures how many fields a query selects in total

cards.subject: Query complexity analysis
says: assigns a cost to each field and rejects queries above a budget
can multiply cost by list-size arguments such as first
cards.use: need to stop a shallow query that still asks for huge lists
not: counts only how deep the query is nested

cards.subject: Persisted queries
says: replace the query text with an identifier the server already knows
reduce request size and permit GET requests
cards.use: want small requests that a CDN can cache
not: require the client to send the full query every time

cards.subject: Automatic persisted queries
says: register a query hash when the server reports it missing
retry the request with the full text on a cache miss
cards.use: want persisted queries without a build-time registration step
not: need all queries to be registered before deployment

cards.subject: Query batching
says: sends several operations in one HTTP request as an array
can hide the real operation count from per-request rate limits
cards.use: want to cut round trips by combining unrelated operations
not: merges the operations into one query with shared variables

cards.subject: Cost-based rate limiting
says: limits clients by the computed cost of their queries
treats a small cheap request and a huge nested one differently
cards.use: find request counts a poor measure of load
not: counts every request as identical

cards.subject: Resolver tracing
says: records timings per resolver to reveal slow fields
helps find which field causes a slow query
cards.use: need to find which field makes one query slow
not: changes how resolvers are executed

cards.subject: Look-ahead fetching
says: uses the selected sub-fields to join or select needed columns in one query
can remove an N+1 without a loader
cards.use: want the parent resolver to load related rows in a single database call
not: ignores which fields the client selected

cards.subject: Offset pagination
says: uses skip and limit or page numbers
can skip or repeat items when rows are inserted between requests
usually gets slower as the offset grows
cards.use: need simple numbered pages over data that rarely changes
not: stays stable while new items are inserted

cards.subject: Cursor pagination
says: uses a position marker to fetch the next page
stays stable when items are inserted or removed during paging
cards.use: page through a feed that changes while the user scrolls
not: identifies a page by its number

cards.subject: A connection
says: wraps a list in edges and page information
is the standard Relay shape for paginated fields
cards.use: want a list field that pages by cursor
not: is a plain array of nodes

cards.subject: An edge
says: pairs a node with its cursor
can hold extra data about the relationship
cards.use: need to attach the cursor or relationship data to one list item
not: reports whether more pages exist

cards.subject: PageInfo
says: reports hasNextPage, hasPreviousPage, startCursor and endCursor
tells the client whether to request another page
cards.use: need to know if there is another page to load
not: holds the list items themselves

cards.subject: The first and after arguments
says: request the first N items after a given cursor
are used to move forward through a connection
cards.use: want the next ten items following the last cursor received
not: page backwards from a cursor

cards.subject: The last and before arguments
says: request the last N items before a given cursor
are used to move backward through a connection
cards.use: need to page backwards from a known cursor
not: move forward through a connection

cards.subject: An opaque cursor
says: should be treated by clients as a meaningless string
lets the server change its encoding without breaking clients
cards.use: want freedom to change how positions are encoded
not: is a number the client may compute

cards.subject: A totalCount field
says: is a common extra on connections but not part of the standard shape
can be expensive to compute on large tables
cards.use: must show the number of matches next to a paged list
not: is required by the connection specification

cards.subject: Keyset pagination
says: turns a cursor into a WHERE clause on an indexed sort key
avoids the cost of scanning skipped rows
cards.use: need fast deep paging over a large indexed table
not: counts and discards the skipped rows

cards.subject: Global object identification
says: gives every object an id unique across types
adds a node field that fetches any object by that id
cards.use: want clients to refetch any object using only its id
not: uses a separate endpoint for each type

cards.subject: The errors array
says: lists problems found while processing a request
sits at the top level beside data in the response
cards.use: want to see why a field failed
not: is returned inside each field's value

cards.subject: A partial response
says: carries data for some fields and null with errors for others
occurs when a nullable field's resolver fails
cards.use: see a response that is part data and part errors
not: occurs only when the whole request failed

cards.subject: An HTTP 200 carrying errors
says: means the transport succeeded while one or more fields failed
is why clients must inspect the errors key and not only the status code
cards.use: find a monitoring dashboard showing success while users see failures
not: always signals a successful operation

cards.subject: An error path
says: points to the response field that failed
contains field names and list indexes
cards.use: need to locate which list item caused an error
not: names the resolver file and line

cards.subject: Error extensions
says: carry machine-readable details such as a code
are the place for custom data on an error
cards.use: want clients to react to an error code rather than parse a message
not: replace the error message field

cards.subject: A validation error
says: is returned before execution when the document does not match the schema
usually comes with no data key
cards.use: send a query that selects a field that does not exist
not: is raised by the resolver of the failed field

cards.subject: Errors as data
says: models expected failures as types such as a union of success and error objects
lets clients branch on a type with a fragment
cards.use: want clients to handle email-already-taken without parsing strings
not: puts every failure in the top-level errors array
like: A mutation payload with user errors

cards.subject: A mutation payload with user errors
says: returns the changed object together with a list of domain errors
leaves the errors array for unexpected failures
cards.use: need a mutation to report which input fields were invalid
not: throws on every invalid input

cards.subject: Error masking
says: hides internal exception details from clients in production
logs the original error on the server
cards.use: find stack traces or database messages appearing in responses
not: adds more detail to client-visible messages

cards.subject: A nullable field as error boundary
says: limits how far a failure's null spreads
lets the rest of the response survive a failing field
cards.use: want a flaky downstream service to fail only its own field
not: makes any failure remove the whole response

cards.subject: Retrying a mutation
says: is unsafe unless the operation is idempotent or carries an idempotency key
can create duplicates after a timeout
cards.use: see a client retry a create after a network timeout
not: is always safe because mutations are atomic

cards.subject: Introspection
says: lets clients query the schema through the __schema and __type fields
powers docs and autocomplete in developer tools
cards.use: want a tool to list the types and fields of a server
not: is a separate endpoint on the server

cards.subject: Turning off introspection
says: reduces schema discovery but is not access control
does not stop attackers who can guess field names
cards.use: hear that hiding the schema is enough to protect it
not: makes unauthorised queries impossible

cards.subject: Field suggestions
says: leak schema names through did-you-mean validation messages
can reveal fields even when introspection is off
cards.use: find field names leaking from error messages with introspection disabled
not: only appear when introspection is on

cards.subject: Authentication
says: identifies the caller, usually from a token header read when building the context
happens before the resolvers run
cards.use: need to know who is making the request
not: is decided separately by each field

cards.subject: Authorization in resolvers
says: checks whether the caller may see a field or object
must cover every path that reaches the data, not only the top-level field
cards.use: need to restrict a field to its owner
not: is satisfied by checking only the root query

cards.subject: Authorization in the business layer
says: keeps permission rules in one place shared by every resolver and other entry point
avoids copying checks into each resolver
cards.use: want the same rules for GraphQL, REST and background jobs
not: is repeated by hand inside each resolver

cards.subject: Alias-based abuse
says: repeats an expensive field or login attempt many times in one request using aliases
bypasses limits that count requests
cards.use: see hundreds of guesses inside a single HTTP request
not: requires many separate HTTP requests

cards.subject: CSRF on a GraphQL endpoint
says: is possible when the server accepts GET or form-encoded POSTs with cookie authentication
is reduced by requiring a JSON content type
cards.use: run a GraphQL endpoint that authenticates with cookies
not: is impossible because all requests are POST

cards.subject: SQL injection in a resolver
says: still happens when a resolver concatenates an argument into SQL
is prevented by parameterised queries
cards.use: find user input spliced into a database query in resolver code
not: is blocked by the GraphQL type system

cards.subject: A persisted query allowlist
says: executes only registered documents and rejects arbitrary ones
shrinks the attack surface for first-party clients
cards.use: serve only your own apps and want to refuse unknown queries
not: is the same as turning off introspection

cards.subject: Broken object-level authorization
says: occurs when a lookup by id returns any object whose id the caller guesses
is checked per object, not per field type
cards.use: see node(id) return another user's record
not: is prevented by making ids long and random

cards.subject: A bearer token header
says: carries the credential in the Authorization header
keeps secrets out of query text and logs
cards.use: must send a credential to a GraphQL API safely
not: is placed in a query variable named token

cards.subject: HTTP caching of POST queries
says: is generally not applied by browsers and CDNs by default
is why URL-keyed caching helps little with a single endpoint
cards.use: find the CDN not caching a GraphQL API
not: works automatically for every request

cards.subject: GET queries
says: put the query and variables in the URL so caches can key them
are limited by URL length unless persisted queries are used
cards.use: want a CDN to cache a read-only operation
not: are used for mutations as well

cards.subject: A normalized client cache
says: stores objects by type and id and shares them across queries
updates every view that shows an object after one fetch
cards.use: want one edit to refresh the same object everywhere on screen
not: stores each query result as an isolated blob

cards.subject: A document cache
says: stores each whole query result keyed by query and variables
does not share objects between different queries
cards.use: want a simple client cache without identity rules
not: merges objects by id across queries

cards.subject: Server response caching
says: stores whole responses keyed by query and variables
must be partitioned per user for private data
cards.use: serve many identical public queries quickly
not: is safe to share between users for private data

cards.subject: Cache control hints
says: set a max-age on types or fields
produce a response policy equal to the lowest value among fields returned
cards.use: want the server to emit a Cache-Control header for a response
not: use the highest max-age of the fields returned

cards.subject: Field-level caching
says: caches the result of one resolver, for example in Redis
helps when one field is slow but its parent is not
cards.use: have one costly field reused by many queries
not: stores whole HTTP responses

cards.subject: A mutation that returns the changed object
says: updates normalized cache entries by id automatically
avoids a manual refetch
cards.use: want the UI to update after an edit without extra queries
not: leaves cached copies stale until a page reload

cards.subject: A private cache scope
says: keeps personalised responses out of shared caches
is set when a response depends on the caller
cards.use: cache a response that includes the current user's data
not: allows a CDN to serve it to everyone

cards.subject: Federation
says: composes several services' graphs into one unified schema
lets teams own separate parts of one graph
cards.use: want many teams to contribute to one client-facing graph
not: merges all services into a single deployable

cards.subject: A subgraph
says: is one service that owns part of the overall graph
publishes its own schema to be composed
cards.use: need to describe a single team's service in a federated graph
not: is what clients query directly

cards.subject: A supergraph
says: is the composed schema clients see
is produced by combining all subgraph schemas
cards.use: want the unified schema that front-end teams use
not: is a single service that holds all data

cards.subject: A router
says: receives client queries and plans how to fetch them from subgraphs
combines the subgraph results into one response
cards.use: need a front door that fans a query out to services
not: stores the business data itself

cards.subject: A query plan
says: lists the subgraph fetches and the order they depend on
is produced by the router for each operation
cards.use: want to understand why one query calls several services
not: is written by hand for each client

cards.subject: An entity
says: is an object type shared across subgraphs and identified by key fields
can have fields contributed by more than one subgraph
cards.use: need a User type with data owned by different teams
not: is limited to a single subgraph

cards.subject: The @key directive
says: declares the fields that uniquely identify an entity
lets other subgraphs reference the entity
cards.use: want to share a type across services using its id
not: marks a field as deprecated

cards.subject: A reference resolver
says: loads an entity from its key representation inside the owning subgraph
is called when the router asks for entity fields
cards.use: need a subgraph to resolve a User given only an id
not: resolves the root Query fields of the router

cards.subject: Schema stitching
says: merges schemas at a gateway through hand-written configuration
puts the merge logic in the gateway rather than in each service
cards.use: combine existing schemas without changes to the services
not: relies on directives declared by each service

cards.subject: Composition
says: checks that subgraph schemas fit together
fails when subgraphs define conflicting types
cards.use: find out whether independent subgraph schemas can be merged
not: runs on every client request

cards.subject: The @external directive
says: marks a field as owned by another subgraph but referenced locally
is used together with requires or provides
cards.use: need a subgraph to mention a field it does not own
not: hides a field from clients

cards.subject: A GraphQL BFF
says: sits in front of existing REST services to give one client-facing graph
adapts several back ends to one frontend's needs
cards.use: have many REST services and one app needing a single graph
not: replaces the REST services entirely

cards.subject: An additive change
says: adds new fields, types or optional arguments
does not break existing clients
cards.use: want to ship a schema change with no client impact
not: removes an existing field

cards.subject: The @deprecated directive
says: marks a field or enum value as obsolete with a reason
keeps the field working while tools warn about it
cards.use: need to retire a field without breaking clients today
not: deletes the field from responses

cards.subject: A breaking change
says: removes or renames a field, or makes an argument required
can fail existing client queries
cards.use: must decide whether a change is safe for deployed apps
not: adds an optional field

cards.subject: Versionless evolution
says: evolves one schema continuously instead of publishing v2 URLs
relies on additive changes and deprecation
cards.use: want to avoid numbered API versions
not: requires a new endpoint for each change

cards.subject: Field usage tracking
says: shows which clients still request a deprecated field
tells you when a field is safe to remove
cards.use: need evidence before removing a deprecated field
not: lists fields no schema defines

cards.subject: Changing nullability
says: can break clients when an output field loosens or an input argument tightens
must be reviewed like a type change
cards.use: plan to turn a non-null output field into a nullable one
not: is always backward compatible

cards.subject: Adding an enum value
says: can break clients that switch exhaustively over the enum
is additive in the schema but not always in client code
cards.use: add a new status to an enum used by mobile apps
not: is always safe for every client

cards.subject: Schema checks in CI
says: diff a proposed schema against the registry and observed traffic
flag breaking changes before merge
cards.use: want builds to fail on unsafe schema changes
not: run only after deployment

cards.subject: Schema-first design
says: starts from SDL and then writes resolvers to match
makes the schema a contract reviewed separately from code
cards.use: want product and front-end teams to review the API before code exists
not: generates the schema from resolver classes

cards.subject: Code-first design
says: builds the schema from definitions written in the host language
generates the SDL as an output
cards.use: want types and schema to come from one set of code definitions
not: starts from a hand-written SDL file

cards.subject: GraphQL naming conventions
says: use camelCase for fields, PascalCase for types and uppercase snake case for enum values
keep schemas readable for every consuming team
cards.use: need a consistent style for a new schema
not: require snake_case for fields

cards.subject: Over-fetching
says: means receiving more fields than the client uses
is reduced in GraphQL because clients choose the fields
cards.use: find a mobile screen downloading unused fields
not: means asking for too few fields

cards.subject: Under-fetching
says: forces multiple round trips to assemble one screen
is a common reason to move to GraphQL
cards.use: need several REST calls to render one page
not: returns too many fields in one call

cards.subject: The single GraphQL endpoint
says: routes every operation through one URL, typically over POST
puts the operation in the request body
cards.use: look for the URL of a GraphQL API
not: uses a different URL for each resource

cards.subject: A typed schema contract
says: documents and validates every operation
lets tools generate types and docs
cards.use: want clients and servers to agree on exact shapes
not: is optional and unchecked by the server

cards.subject: HTTP status codes in GraphQL
says: mostly report transport problems, not field-level outcomes
are less expressive than REST codes such as 404 or 409
cards.use: see a failed record lookup returning 200
not: map one-to-one to every field error

cards.subject: File upload in GraphQL
says: is not defined by the core specification
is often handled by a multipart extension or signed URLs
cards.use: need to send a file through an API
not: is built into the query language as a scalar

cards.subject: REST resource URLs
says: let HTTP caches and CDNs key responses by URL
are shaped by the server for each resource
cards.use: want standard HTTP caching with no extra machinery
not: need a persisted query to be cached

cards.subject: Many clients with differing data needs
says: favour GraphQL when web, mobile and partners want different slices
benefit from clients choosing their own fields
cards.use: serve web, mobile and partner apps from one API
not: favour a fixed REST payload

cards.subject: Simple CRUD with one client
says: often favours REST for its simplicity and caching
needs less machinery than a GraphQL server
cards.use: build a small internal service with a single consuming app
not: requires GraphQL for typed contracts

cards.subject: Server-side complexity
says: shifts to the server in GraphQL through resolvers, batching and cost limits
is the price paid for client flexibility
cards.use: weigh the operational cost of running a GraphQL server
not: disappears when clients choose their own fields

cards.subject: Apollo Client
says: is a GraphQL client with a normalized in-memory cache
offers hooks such as useQuery for React
cards.use: want a full-featured React client with a normalized cache
not: is a GraphQL server implementation

cards.subject: urql
says: is a lighter GraphQL client built around a pipeline of exchanges
caches whole documents by default with an optional normalized cache
cards.use: want a small, extensible client where caching is a pluggable exchange
not: requires a compiler step for every query

cards.subject: Relay
says: expects fragments colocated with components and a compiler step
uses connections and global ids by convention
cards.use: build a large React app with strict data-masking conventions
not: works with any schema shape without conventions

cards.subject: A fetch policy
says: chooses between cache and network for each query
includes options such as cache-first and network-only
cards.use: need a screen to always show fresh data
not: is set once for the whole schema on the server

cards.subject: Fragment colocation
says: keeps each component's data needs next to the component
lets a parent compose children's fragments into one query
cards.use: want components to declare exactly the data they use
not: puts every query in one central file

cards.subject: An optimistic response
says: shows the expected result in the UI before the server confirms
rolls back if the mutation fails
cards.use: want instant feedback when a user likes a post
not: waits for the server before updating the UI

cards.subject: Polling
says: re-runs a query on a fixed interval
needs no persistent connection
cards.use: want periodic refresh without WebSockets
not: pushes updates from the server instantly

cards.subject: Network error versus GraphQL error
says: separates a failed transport from field errors in a response
needs different handling in the client
cards.use: need to tell offline from a resolver failure
not: are the same thing in all clients

cards.subject: Query deduplication
says: sends one network request when identical queries fire at once
shares the result with all waiting components
cards.use: see many components asking for the same data on mount
not: merges different queries into one

cards.subject: A cache merge function
says: tells the client how to combine pages of a list into one cache field
is needed for infinite scroll with cursors
cards.use: load more pages and see the cache replacing earlier items
not: replaces the earlier items with each new page

cards.subject: Server-sent events
says: carry one-way server push over plain HTTP
can serve as a transport for subscriptions
cards.use: want subscriptions without WebSockets
not: offer two-way messaging on one socket

cards.subject: GraphiQL
says: is an in-browser IDE for writing and running queries
uses introspection for docs and autocomplete
cards.use: want to try queries against a server from the browser
not: is a production client library

cards.subject: A plain HTTP POST request
says: carries JSON with query, variables and an optional operation name
works from curl or any HTTP library
cards.use: need to call a GraphQL server without a client library
not: sends the query as a form field named document

cards.subject: GraphQL Code Generator
says: generates typed code from the schema and operations
keeps client types in step with the schema
cards.use: want TypeScript types derived from queries
not: hosts the GraphQL server

cards.subject: Schema linting
says: enforces naming, description and style rules on the schema
runs in CI beside schema checks
cards.use: need to keep a large schema consistent across teams
not: executes queries against test data

cards.subject: graphql-js
says: is the reference implementation in JavaScript
exposes a graphql function that executes a query against a schema
cards.use: need to run a query against a schema inside a test
not: is a React client library

cards.subject: A resolver unit test
says: calls a resolver directly with mock parent, args and context
runs fast with no HTTP
cards.use: want to check one resolver's logic alone
not: boots the full HTTP server

cards.subject: A schema execution test
says: runs a real query document against the schema with test data
covers resolvers wired together
cards.use: verify that fields, arguments and resolvers work together
not: calls the resolver function with no schema

cards.subject: An end-to-end HTTP test
says: posts to the real endpoint to cover auth middleware and context creation
catches wiring that schema-level tests skip
cards.use: need to confirm headers and context reach resolvers
not: calls resolvers directly

cards.subject: A schema snapshot test
says: prints the SDL and fails on unplanned changes
makes schema edits visible in review
cards.use: want an unintended type change to fail a test
not: checks resolver outputs

cards.subject: Schema mocking
says: returns generated fake data for each type from the schema alone
lets front-end teams work before the back end exists
cards.use: want a front-end team to build against a not-yet-implemented API
not: calls the real database

cards.subject: gglearn and ggsocial APIs
says: are REST-style Next.js route handlers, not GraphQL
are validated per route with a schema library
cards.use: look for a GraphQL server in our apps
not: serve a single GraphQL endpoint

cards.subject: The ggsocial GitHub adapter
says: consumes GitHub's GraphQL endpoint to create Discussions
sends a POST whose JSON holds a query and variables
authenticates with a fine-grained personal access token sent as Bearer
cards.use: see how our code calls a GraphQL API
not: exposes a GraphQL schema of its own

cards.subject: GitHub node IDs
says: are required for the repository and category in createDiscussion
are the reason the adapter's form asks the operator for them
cards.use: configure the GitHub Discussions adapter
not: are optional because names are accepted instead

cards.subject: The createDiscussion mutation
says: takes a CreateDiscussionInput with repository, category, title and body
asks back only the new discussion's id and url
cards.use: see what the adapter requests back from GitHub
not: returns the full discussion thread

cards.subject: The adapter's errors check
says: reads the errors array and throws instead of trusting the HTTP status
exists because GraphQL can answer 200 with errors
cards.use: find why the adapter inspects the response body
not: relies on 4xx and 5xx codes alone

cards.subject: Moksy's integration catalogue entries
says: list GraphQL among API styles
note that products such as monday.com and Upwork offer GraphQL APIs
cards.use: check what Moksy docs say about GraphQL
not: describe Moksy as a GraphQL provider

cards.subject: Our REST-or-GraphQL choice
says: favours route handlers because the clients are our own UI and a few agents
treats GraphQL as a topic for integration, not for serving
cards.use: explain why our stack avoids a GraphQL server
not: follows from a lack of typed schemas

cards.subject: Checking for a REST alternative
says: comes before wiring a GraphQL call, as GitHub offers REST for issues and releases
often gives a simpler and safer integration
cards.use: plan to integrate with a third-party GraphQL API
not: is unnecessary when a provider has GraphQL

qa.q: What does the exclamation mark mean in this field?
qa.right: The server promises never to return null for email
wrong: The argument must be sent as a variable
The field is computed by a mutation
qa.why: A trailing ! marks the type as non-null.

qa.q: What is the shape of the JSON a server returns for this query on success?
qa.right: An object with a data key whose user object holds only name
wrong: An object with a user key holding every field of User
An array of rows, one per column of the users table
qa.why: The response mirrors the shape of the selection set under a data key.

qa.q: Which three kinds of operation does GraphQL define?
qa.right: Query, mutation and subscription
wrong: Read, write and stream, each at its own endpoint
qa.why: The spec defines query, mutation and subscription operations.

qa.q: How does a client usually send a GraphQL operation over HTTP?
qa.right: A POST to a single endpoint with JSON holding query and variables
wrong: A PUT to /graphql/query with the SDL as the body
A GET to a different URL for each field
A POST to one URL per type with form fields named by column
qa.why: The standard transport is one endpoint carrying a JSON body.

qa.q: What is wrong with how this client builds the request?
qa.right: User input is spliced into the query text, which allows injection and defeats caching
wrong: Template strings are not allowed in JavaScript
The id must be sent as a number
Queries must always be sent with GET
qa.why: Declare variables and send them in the variables map instead of gluing strings.
qa.code:
const query = `{ user(id: "${userInput}") { name } }`;
await fetch("/graphql", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify({ query }) });

qa.q: What does the type of the field posts mean?
qa.right: The list may not be null and no item in it may be null
wrong: The list may be null but its items may not
Each item may be null but the list itself may not
Both the list and the items may be null
qa.why: [Post!]! is a non-null list of non-null Post items.

qa.q: Why does this query need aliases?
qa.right: Two selections of the same field with different arguments would otherwise clash in the response
wrong: Aliases make the query run in parallel
Aliases are needed whenever a field has an argument
Aliases hide the fields from introspection
qa.why: The response key defaults to the field name, so a second selection needs a different key.

qa.q: What does the fragment spread do?
qa.right: Includes the fields from UserBits in that selection
wrong: Sends UserBits as a separate request
Imports the UserBits type from another schema
qa.why: A fragment names a reusable set of fields that is spread with three dots.

qa.q: What does this response tell you?
qa.right: The user field failed and is null, while the request itself was processed and reported the error
wrong: The query had a syntax error and nothing ran
The user was found but has no name
qa.why: Execution errors appear in the errors array next to data, often with HTTP 200.

qa.q: Why does this mutation take one input object?
qa.right: It keeps the mutation signature stable as fields are added and groups related arguments
wrong: A mutation cannot take scalar arguments
Input objects are required to make the mutation run serially
It lets the mutation return a list
qa.why: One input type and one payload type allow additive evolution.

qa.q: What is this introspection query asking?
qa.right: For the names of the types in the schema
wrong: For the rows stored in the database
For the list of running subscriptions
qa.why: __schema is the entry point of the schema's self-description.

qa.q: What value does limit take when the client sends no variables?
qa.why: A variable default is used when the client does not supply the variable.

qa.q: A page of 50 posts shows 51 database queries in the log. What is happening and what fixes it?
qa.right: N+1 from a per-post author resolver; batch the author lookups with a DataLoader
wrong: The query is too deep; add a depth limit
The cache is cold; enable response caching
Mutations are running serially; make them parallel
qa.why: One list query plus one lookup per item is the N+1 pattern, solved by batching keys.

qa.q: How should the author resolver use the loader?
qa.right: Call the loader per post and let it batch all keys of the tick into one lookup
wrong: Create a new loader inside the resolver for each post
Call the batch function directly for each post
Await each loader call before starting the next post
qa.why: Calls made in the same tick are collected and sent to the batch function once.

qa.q: What must this batch function return for the loader to work?
qa.right: An array of users in the same order and length as the keys, with null or an error for missing ones
wrong: Only the users that were found, in database order
A single object keyed by id
A promise that resolves after the first key
qa.why: A DataLoader batch function maps the keys array to a values array positionally.

qa.q: How do you read the title of a SearchResult that may be a Post or a User?
qa.right: Use an inline fragment per member type
wrong: Select title directly because every union shares it
Add an @include directive on the union
Query SearchResult twice with two aliases
qa.why: Fields of union members are only selectable inside a type condition.

qa.q: What cursor should the client send to load the next page?
qa.right: The endCursor from pageInfo of the last page
wrong: The cursor of the first edge
The total count returned by the server
qa.why: Forward paging uses after with the last page's end cursor.

qa.q: A feed using skip and limit shows repeated items when new posts arrive while the user scrolls. What should the team do?
qa.right: Move to cursor-based pagination so the position does not shift
wrong: Add a depth limit to the query
qa.why: Offset pages shift when rows are inserted; a cursor anchors to an item.

qa.q: Monitoring shows only 200 responses but customers report failures. What should you check first?
qa.right: Whether the errors array in the response bodies is being counted
wrong: Whether the CDN is returning stale GET responses
Whether the schema uses too many unions
qa.why: GraphQL execution errors are normally returned with HTTP 200.

qa.q: What does this directive do for clients?
qa.right: Marks the field as obsolete while keeping it working and shows the reason in tooling
qa.why: @deprecated is a signal, not a removal.

qa.q: The team wants a CDN to cache read-only queries. What is the usual approach?
qa.right: Use persisted query ids sent with GET so the URL is cacheable
qa.why: A short id in the URL avoids URL length limits and lets caches key the request.

qa.q: A public API is slowed by queries nesting friends of friends many levels deep. What controls fit?
qa.right: A depth limit plus query cost analysis
qa.why: Depth and cost limits bound how much work one query can request.
qa.code: { me { friends { friends { friends { name } } } } }

qa.q: Where should the authenticated user be placed so every resolver can use it?
qa.right: On the context created once per request
wrong: In a global variable shared by all requests
In each resolver's arguments sent by the client
qa.why: The context is per request and shared by resolvers.
qa.code:
const server = new ApolloServer({ schema });
// context: async ({ req }) => ({ user: await auth(req.headers.authorization) })

qa.q: The author field is non-null and its resolver throws. What does the client get?
qa.right: The nearest nullable parent becomes null and an error is reported
wrong: The whole response is replaced by an HTTP 500
The error is swallowed with no entry in errors
qa.why: A null from a non-null field propagates up to the first nullable ancestor.

qa.q: A developer says the schema is secure because introspection is disabled in production. What is the right response?
qa.right: It only hides discovery; field-level authorization and cost limits are still required
wrong: Correct, guessing field names is impractical
Correct, validation rejects unknown fields so no data can leak
Incorrect, because introspection must stay on for tokens to work
qa.why: Hiding the schema is not access control.

qa.q: Your code must call a third-party GraphQL API. Which practice is right?
qa.right: Send variables, use a scoped token in a header, and check the errors array
wrong: Build the query by concatenating user input
Put the token in the query text
Trust the HTTP status and ignore the body
qa.why: Treat it like any third-party API and do not trust a 200.

qa.q: A small internal tool has one front end and simple CRUD. What is the sensible API style?
qa.right: REST route handlers are likely enough
wrong: GraphQL is required for typed APIs
qa.why: Choose by the problem; simple needs favour less machinery.

qa.q: A client sends a variable declared as ID! but omits it. What happens?
qa.right: The request is rejected with an error before any resolver runs
wrong: The resolver receives null and runs
The server substitutes an empty string
qa.why: Required variables are checked when variables are coerced.

qa.q: Resolvers check the role only on the top-level adminReport field. A customer can read the same data through user -> reports. What is the flaw?
qa.right: Authorization is not applied on every path to the data
wrong: The schema has too many types
qa.why: Checks belong on the data or in a shared layer so every path is covered.

qa.q: Why does this request evade a limit of five login attempts per request count?
qa.right: Aliases repeat the mutation many times inside one HTTP request
qa.why: Rate limit by operation cost or count executed fields, not just requests.

qa.q: What does @key tell a federated router?
qa.right: Which fields identify an entity so other subgraphs can reference it
wrong: Which client may query the type
qa.why: The key is how entities are looked up across subgraphs.

qa.q: A mobile app still uses the field fullName. What should you do before removing it?
qa.right: Deprecate it, track usage and remove it only when no clients request it
wrong: Delete it and rely on validation errors
Rename it and keep the old name in the docs
qa.why: Removal is breaking; deprecation plus usage tracking makes it safe.

qa.q: After the team added a PENDING enum value, an older client crashes. Why?
qa.right: Its code switched exhaustively over the enum and has no case for the new value
wrong: The server renamed the old values
qa.why: An additive schema change can still break exhaustive client logic.

qa.q: How should a signup mutation report that the email is already taken?
qa.right: Return an error type or userErrors field the client can branch on
wrong: Throw an exception and let the client parse the message
Return null for the whole payload
qa.why: Expected failures are better modelled as data than as top-level errors.

qa.q: Users sometimes see each other's cached rows. What is the likely bug?
qa.right: The DataLoader is created at module scope and shared across requests
wrong: The loader batch function returns too many values
qa.why: Create loaders per request so their cache does not cross users.
qa.code:
const userLoader = new DataLoader(batchUsers);
export const context = async () => ({ userLoader });

qa.q: Why is a first value of 100 on both nesting levels dangerous?
qa.right: It can request up to ten thousand comments in one query
qa.why: Cost multiplies across nested lists, so a cost analysis must multiply by first.

qa.q: A server accepts GET queries and form-encoded POSTs and authenticates by cookie. What risk does this create?
qa.right: Cross-site request forgery from another site
qa.why: Requiring a JSON content type or custom header blocks simple cross-site requests.

qa.q: After an edit mutation, the item list in the UI still shows old data. What is the usual cause with a normalized cache?
qa.right: The mutation did not return the changed object with its id and type
wrong: The query used too many aliases
qa.why: The normalized cache updates entries by id when the response includes them.

qa.q: A single call to the schema is made in a test. Which test level is this?
qa.right: A schema execution test that runs a real document against the schema
wrong: A snapshot test of the SDL
qa.why: graphql() executes the document through validation and resolvers without HTTP.

qa.q: Which tool helps you find why one query is slow?
qa.right: Per-resolver tracing
qa.why: Tracing records timing per field.

qa.q: Two mutations are written in one document. In what order do they run?
qa.right: One after the other, in the order written
wrong: In the order the server prefers
The second runs only if the first fails
qa.why: Top-level mutation fields execute serially.

qa.q: A team has many REST services and a new app needs one graph. What is a reasonable first step?
qa.right: Build a GraphQL layer that wraps the REST services
wrong: Federate nothing and call REST directly
Move the data to the client
qa.why: A GraphQL BFF can adapt existing services without rewriting them.

qa.q: An unauthenticated connection to a subscription should be handled how?
qa.right: Validate the token when the connection is made and reject if invalid
wrong: Accept it and check once the first event arrives
qa.why: Authentication must be checked at connection time and enforced per event.

qa.q: Why can node(id:) be risky?
qa.right: It can return any object whose id is guessed unless each object is authorised
qa.why: Lookups by id need object-level authorization.

qa.q: A client of a federated graph is slow because the router calls the products subgraph once per item. What is the likely cause and fix?
qa.right: The reference resolver loads each entity separately; batch entity lookups with a loader
wrong: The router lacks a cache; add a depth limit
The key is missing; remove it
qa.why: Entity resolution is another N+1 point and needs batching.

qa.q: A public API wants to accept only the company's own apps. What control fits best?
qa.right: A persisted query allowlist
qa.why: Only registered documents are executed.

qa.q: A totalCount field times out on a 50 million row table. What should be done?
qa.right: Make it optional, approximate or separate, or drop it
wrong: Convert the connection to an offset list
qa.why: Counts are costly; offer them only when affordable.

qa.q: A schema returns an unbounded list. Which design fix is best?
qa.right: Return a connection with a maximum page size
qa.why: Unbounded lists invite abuse.

qa.q: Which type allows null items but not a null list?
qa.right: [Post]!
qa.why: The outer ! applies to the list; the inner type is nullable.

qa.q: A mutation timed out and the client retries it automatically. What is the risk?
qa.right: Duplicate side effects unless the mutation is idempotent or uses a key
qa.why: Retries need idempotency.

qa.q: A query is rejected because the cursor was edited by a client. What design principle was violated?
qa.right: Cursors should be treated as opaque
wrong: Cursors must be sent as headers
Cursors may only be used with mutations
qa.why: Clients must not interpret or build cursors.

qa.q: A response for a personalised page is cached on the CDN. What went wrong?
qa.right: The response lacked a private cache scope
qa.why: Personalised data must not be stored in shared caches.
